correctness.rationale: The selected stems depend on disjoint independent sets of tips. Their Bernoulli variances add and differentiation gives k(1-p)^(k-1)[2(1-p)^k-1] for each unit squared-length coefficient. A new stem of length k^(-1/4) contributes order sqrt(k) at p=c/k with limiting signed coefficient e^(-c)(2e^(-c)-1), positive at c=1/4 and negative at c=1, while old terms are bounded there. At old positive endpoints the new derivative tends to zero exponentially, so induction preserves disjoint strict sign brackets. A binary scaffold has the clades as pendant subtrees; for one clade one may put a spare tip across the root so that the clade has an incoming stem. Assigning small positive lengths to all remaining edges preserves the derivative brackets by finite polynomial dependence. In each bracket an interior maximizer exists and is strict, since the variance polynomial is nonconstant and any fixed level has only finitely many preimages. The mean formula is an edge sum of nondecreasing concave functions. For the 100,514-tip example, integer interval multiplication and squaring (outward rounding at scale 10^32, independent of the supplied Decimal verifier) reproduce derivative pairs approximately (+0.9296875,-0.5), (+15.89502604,-1.14168436), (+203.51060288,-4.46131721), with certified margins at least 1/2. Differentiating the Bernoulli product law gives a sum of n conditional-expectation differences, each bounded by the range width. Applied to 2XZ+Z^2 and 2 EX EZ+(EZ)^2 this gives 6nLη+3nη², independently checked to be less than 1.60e-7. The original six signs therefore persist.
residual_risks: Proof concerns at least m peaks and does not count all critical points. Positive lengths are not constrained to be ultrametric. No claim for correlated extinction or rarefaction.

originality.rationale: The classical variance identity and the existence of two peaks are prior. The surviving distinct claim is unbounded peak count in the strictly positive full binary class, with a certified three-peak witness. Neither the prior two-peak construction nor the exact moment framework itself supplies this conclusion.
residual_risks: A construction for separated-scale Bernoulli sums outside phylogenetic indexing or an equivalent unindexed example may remain. Literature coverage is bounded, not priority certification.

value.rationale: The prior two-peak examples rule out unimodality only; this construction rules out every universal finite modal bound while retaining binary topology, positive lengths and homogeneous survival. It distinguishes the complexity of variance from the simple concave mean, and supplies finite parameters with a sign margin rather than relying on plotted peaks.
residual_risks: Separated clade sizes and tiny other lengths are existence devices; empirical prevalence and near-ultrametric behavior are unestablished.
